methodology.title: Election equipment catalog evidence policy
methodology.description: The pilot records what an official source actually establishes and keeps certified configurations, state approvals, jurisdiction deployment observations, historical configuration changes, and unknown field details in separate scopes.
methodology.caveat: An EAC engineering change order documents an approved change to one or more certified configurations. It does not establish that a particular jurisdiction installed the change, and a VSTL record is not a unit-level service or repair history.

systems.summary: A source-linked dossier for the ClearAccess ballot-marking configuration within EAC-certified ClearVote 2.5, including named COTS components, explicit external UPS options, certified software observations, and Pro V&V test findings.

certification.caveat: EAC certification applies only to the evaluated ClearVote 2.5 certified configuration. It does not establish which permitted ClearAccess options a jurisdiction selected or what is installed in a particular fielded unit.

components.name: ClearAccess software
components.description: The certified scope lists proprietary ClearAccess software version 2.5.6 and its configured COTS software environment.
components.caveat: These are versions in the certified configuration, not a live reading from a deployed workstation and not a claim that 2.5.6 is the newest product-family release.

components.name: All-in-one touchscreen computer
components.description: The certified scope permits ELO 15-inch EloPOS and E-Series or X-Series all-in-one touchscreens, plus a Dell OptiPlex 5250 option. The reference scene follows Clear Ballot's official portrait Elo product image.
components.caveat: The computers are alternatives. Dell specifications are restricted to the OptiPlex 5250 family, and the official portrait Elo product image is not treated as proof of which certified Elo model or internal configuration it depicts.

technicalSpecifications.label: Certified touchscreen alternatives
technicalSpecifications.value: Elo EPS15E2, ESY15E2, ESY20X2; Dell OptiPlex 5250
technicalSpecifications.caveat: These are alternatives, not a single combined hardware configuration and not evidence of a jurisdiction's selected model.

technicalSpecifications.label: CPU options
technicalSpecifications.value: Intel 6th/7th Generation Pentium, Core i3 dual-core, or Core i5/i7 quad-core product-family options
technicalSpecifications.caveat: Pro V&V identifies the OptiPlex 5250 as an option; Dell lists configurable processor choices. The exact processor in a certified or fielded ClearAccess unit is not established.

technicalSpecifications.label: RAM
technicalSpecifications.value: Two DDR4 SODIMM slots; up to 32 GB product-family maximum
technicalSpecifications.caveat: This is capacity supported by the Dell product family, not the installed RAM in a certified or fielded ClearAccess computer.

technicalSpecifications.label: Storage
technicalSpecifications.value: 2.5-inch bay plus M.2 SSD connector; HDD, hybrid-drive, SATA/PCIe SSD, and dual-storage product-family options
technicalSpecifications.caveat: The exact installed drive type and capacity for the certified ClearAccess option are not established by the reviewed sources.

technicalSpecifications.label: USB ports
technicalSpecifications.value: 6 external: 4 × USB 3.1 Gen 1 and 2 × USB 2.0
technicalSpecifications.caveat: This is the physical connector count for the Dell alternative, not for the Elo alternatives and not proof of port occupation or enabled devices.

technicalSpecifications.label: Ethernet
technicalSpecifications.value: Integrated Intel I219-V 10/100/1000 Ethernet; 1 rear RJ-45
technicalSpecifications.caveat: Physical Ethernet capability does not establish a connected, enabled, or field-used election network.

technicalSpecifications.label: Cellular modem
technicalSpecifications.caveat: No cellular modem is identified for the reviewed alternatives. Dell lists optional Wi-Fi/Bluetooth for its general product family, but that is not proof of an installed certified ClearAccess radio or of field use.

technicalSpecifications.label: Elo CPU, RAM, and storage
technicalSpecifications.caveat: The reviewed immutable artifacts establish the Elo model alternatives and an external reference image but do not provide a safely attributable exact CPU, installed RAM, or storage configuration for those certified variants.

components.name: Ballot printer
components.description: The certified scope lists Oki Data B432dn and Lexmark MS521dn or MS531dw laser-printer options for ClearAccess.
components.caveat: These are certified alternatives, not evidence that all three printers are present in one configuration or that a particular jurisdiction uses one of them.

components.name: External uninterruptible power supply
components.description: The certified scope lists CyberPower PR1500RT2U and APC SMT2200C or SRT1500RMXLA UPS models for ClearAccess.
components.caveat: The source confirms permitted UPS models but does not state battery capacity, runtime under a ClearAccess load, field topology, maintenance condition, or the option selected by a jurisdiction.

components.name: Accessible keypad
components.description: The reviewed scope and test plan list Storm EZ Access keypad models as accessible input devices for ClearAccess.
components.caveat: The records list approved or evaluated keypad alternatives; they do not identify the model connected to a particular unit.

components.name: Barcode scanner
components.description: The certified scope lists Zebra DS457-SR and ELO UM600149 barcode-scanner options for ClearAccess.
components.caveat: The sources establish certified alternatives, not the scanner attached to a fielded ClearAccess configuration.

components.name: Sip-and-puff and audio accessories
components.description: The Pro V&V physical configuration audit lists Origin Instruments BZ2 and BZ2U sip-and-puff devices and Samson SASR350 headphones with the ClearAccess test components.
components.caveat: The test-plan PCA documents components submitted for evaluation. It does not establish that these accessories are packaged with or connected to every deployed setup.

components.name: ESD and EMI control materials
components.description: The certified scope lists copper tape, acrylic and polyimide films, and named ferrite parts under ClearAccess COTS hardware.
components.caveat: The schematic marker is only a selection aid. The public scope does not establish the exact quantity, placement, routing, or physical appearance of these materials in a particular setup.

components.name: Transportation and setup case
components.description: The test plan lists case models 62311-1-1 and 62312-1-1 for the ClearAccess touchscreen, printer, headphones, keypad, and associated cables.
components.caveat: A tested transportation option does not establish a jurisdiction's storage, transport, setup, or chain-of-custody procedure.

versionObservations.label: EAC-certified ClearAccess software
versionObservations.caveat: This is the software version in the certified ClearVote 2.5 configuration, not a live device reading or a claim about the newest ClearVote release.

versionObservations.label: Certified COTS operating-system environment
versionObservations.caveat: The scope lists the certified software environment; it does not establish patch state or configuration on a fielded computer.

configurationChanges.description: ClearAccess automatically rolls the system log when more than 1,000 log entries are present to reduce performance risk.
configurationChanges.caveat: The change appears in the submitted ClearVote 2.5 certification modification set. It does not establish installation on a particular fielded unit.

configurationChanges.description: ClearAccess and ClearCast received minor libssl and OpenSSL version updates in the submitted modification set.
configurationChanges.caveat: This is certification configuration history, not evidence of a field update, patch installation date, or current exposure on any unit.

configurationChanges.description: The ClearAccess 2.5.5 write-in controls did not meet specified touch-area dimensions; the report records the corrected 2.5.6 interface.
configurationChanges.caveat: This is a test-campaign deficiency and resolution, not evidence that version 2.5.5 was used in a public election.

findings.title: ClearAccess 2.5.5 write-in controls were undersized
findings.description: Pro V&V reported that the write-in menu button dimensions and spacing in ClearAccess 2.5.5 did not meet the cited VVSG requirement and documented corrected dimensions and keyboard options in 2.5.6.
findings.caveat: This is a certification-test finding with a reported resolution. It is not evidence that the deficient build was deployed in an election.

findings.title: OpenSSL libraries updated in the submitted modification set
findings.description: The Pro V&V test plan identifies the ClearAccess and ClearCast libssl/OpenSSL update as a bug change addressing CVE-2022-0778.
findings.caveat: The record describes the submitted certified configuration. It is not a field vulnerability scan, a current security assessment, or evidence of exploitation.

findings.title: One anomaly and multiple deficiencies were documented during testing
findings.description: The final Pro V&V report describes one ClearMark anomaly with no determined root cause and lists test deficiencies with reported corrective actions before recommending certification of the submitted system.
findings.caveat: This system-level summary is not a claim that ClearAccess caused the ClearMark anomaly, that findings occurred in the field, or that no other defects exist.

findings.title: The modification had not been fielded when the 2024 test plan was written
findings.description: The Pro V&V test plan stated that the ClearVote 2.5 modification had not been fielded for use as of the plan date.
findings.caveat: This is a historical pre-certification statement. Do not infer that ClearVote 2.5 remained undeployed after certification or is not deployed today.

power.description: The certified ClearVote 2.5 scope names three external UPS options for ClearAccess. The reviewed sources do not provide a ClearAccess load-specific capacity or runtime claim.
power.caveat: Confirmed means the models appear in the certified configuration, not that every jurisdiction uses one, that all are used together, or that battery health and runtime are known for a fielded setup.

scene.assetAttribution: Original CivicResultMaps schematic generated from scripts/build-clearaccess-model.mjs
scene.description: An original, photo-informed navigational schematic using Clear Ballot's portrait Elo ClearAccess product image as the external reference, with separately source-supported printer, UPS, keypad, scanner, and accessibility components.
scene.referenceConfiguration: Portrait Elo ClearAccess product-photo configuration with accessible keypad and headphones; printer and external UPS shown as certified alternative categories
scene.referenceNote: The touchscreen, keypad, and headphone silhouette follows the official product image. The image does not establish which Elo model is pictured, and the printer, UPS, port locations, cabling, and explosion paths remain illustrative.

referenceImages.caption: Manufacturer product image: ClearAccess touchscreen, headphones, and accessible keypad.

caveats: Certified component alternatives are not evidence that all listed options are installed together or that a jurisdiction selected a particular model.
The 3D reference follows an official ClearAccess product photo but remains a selection aid, not vendor CAD, a teardown, a wiring diagram, or proof of exact dimensions and internal placement.
The UPS models are confirmed configuration options, but capacity, load-specific runtime, maintenance condition, and field topology remain unknown.
Test findings are time- and version-scoped. They do not prove a field incident, exploitation, altered votes, fraud, misconduct, or an incorrect election outcome.

systems.summary: A source-linked dossier for the ImageCast X ballot-marking device within EAC-certified Democracy Suite 5.17, including certified device alternatives, external UPS options, version observations, Pro V&V results, and EAC-hosted post-certification advisories.

certification.caveat: EAC certification applies only to the evaluated Democracy Suite 5.17 certified configuration. It does not establish election readiness, a jurisdiction deployment, the option selected for a fielded unit, or the condition of any unit. The certification-era documents name Dominion Voting Systems; the current EAC record separately notes a later Liberty Vote USA acquisition.

components.name: ImageCast X application and configuration
components.description: The final EAC scope lists the ICX application and Android environment, while the Pro V&V plan and report preserve submitted-test and final configuration identifiers.
components.caveat: These are source-scoped certification and test observations, not a live device reading and not a claim about the newest Democracy Suite or ImageCast X release.

components.name: ImageCast X touchscreen BMD computer
components.description: The certified configuration lists Avalue Classic 15-inch and 21-inch tablet options and an Avalue Prime 21-inch option. The reference scene uses the documented SID-21V-Z37-A1R Classic 21.5-inch profile.
components.caveat: The models and chassis are permitted alternatives. The reference scene depicts the SID-21V-Z37-A1R hardware family and must not be read as the Prime variant or as evidence of a jurisdiction's selected hardware.

technicalSpecifications.label: Display and touch panel
technicalSpecifications.value: 21.5-inch, 1920 × 1080, projected-capacitive touch
technicalSpecifications.caveat: The manufacturer specification is tied to the named SID-21V model family. It is not transferred to the 15-inch Classic or 21-inch Prime alternatives.

components.name: SID-21V compute board profile
components.description: The Avalue SID-21V-Z37-A1R manual identifies the processor, memory, and eMMC storage used by the Classic 21.5-inch hardware profile.
components.caveat: The scene makes this documented hardware profile selectable, but its board outline and placement are illustrative. The profile must not be transferred to ICX Prime or a particular fielded unit.

technicalSpecifications.label: CPU
technicalSpecifications.value: Intel Atom Z3735F
technicalSpecifications.caveat: This is the COTS manufacturer specification for the named SID-21V model family, not a live inventory of a jurisdiction unit.

technicalSpecifications.label: RAM
technicalSpecifications.value: 2 GB DDR3L
technicalSpecifications.caveat: This is the COTS manufacturer specification for the named SID-21V model family.

technicalSpecifications.label: Internal storage
technicalSpecifications.value: 32 GB eMMC
technicalSpecifications.caveat: This eMMC specification belongs to the SID-21V Classic profile and is not the source-supported ICX Prime SSD advisory component.

components.name: SID-21V connector panel
components.description: The SID-21V manufacturer manual identifies the model-family connector set. The certified scope separately describes allowed system communications use.
components.caveat: Connector presence is a model-family specification. It does not establish port occupation, enabled services, cabling, or jurisdiction use; the scene location is illustrative.

technicalSpecifications.label: USB ports
technicalSpecifications.caveat: The manual states the physical connector count; it does not establish which ports are occupied or enabled in a fielded election configuration.

technicalSpecifications.label: Ethernet
technicalSpecifications.value: 1 × 10/100 RJ-45 Ethernet
technicalSpecifications.caveat: Physical connector presence does not establish an enabled election network connection or field use.

technicalSpecifications.label: Other documented I/O
technicalSpecifications.value: 1 × HDMI, 1 × headphone jack, 1 × smart-card reader, 1 × microSD slot
technicalSpecifications.caveat: These are hardware-family connectors and peripherals, not proof of a connected accessory or inserted media.

technicalSpecifications.label: Cellular modem
technicalSpecifications.value: No WAN modem or WAN wireless use listed in the Democracy Suite 5.17 certified-system table
technicalSpecifications.caveat: This is a system-scope communications statement, not a teardown-based assertion that every ICX chassis lacks every radio component.

components.name: SID-21V optional internal battery
components.description: The Avalue manual documents an optional rechargeable battery and its hinged top-cover installation path for the SID-21V-Z37-A1R profile.
components.caveat: The component is optional. Its source-supported cover area guides the scene, but the simplified cell-pack geometry is illustrative and no field installation or battery condition is established.

technicalSpecifications.label: Battery pack
technicalSpecifications.value: ACC-BAT-3S1P-01R; rechargeable Li-ion; 10.8 V nominal
technicalSpecifications.caveat: A documented optional accessory is not presumed installed in every certified or fielded ICX.

technicalSpecifications.label: Battery capacity
technicalSpecifications.value: 2,400 mAh typical; 2,215 mAh minimum at the documented test conditions
technicalSpecifications.caveat: Capacity is a manufacturer specification, not runtime under an election workload or a measure of any unit's current battery health.

technicalSpecifications.label: Election-workload runtime
technicalSpecifications.caveat: The reviewed manuals provide electrical capacity and storage guidance but not a source-supported election-workload runtime.

components.name: ImageCast X ballot printer
components.description: The reviewed scope and test records list six laser-printer alternatives for an ICX ballot-marking configuration.
components.caveat: These are certified alternatives, not evidence that all printers appear together or that a particular jurisdiction uses a named model.

components.name: External uninterruptible power supply
components.description: The Pro V&V ICX configuration lists APC and CyberPower external UPS alternatives, and the EAC scope includes the same model families in the certified COTS hardware list.
components.caveat: The sources confirm permitted UPS alternatives but do not provide ICX load-specific capacity or runtime, field topology, battery condition, maintenance status, or a jurisdiction selection.

components.name: Accessible-tactile interface
components.description: The certified hardware list includes ATI-USB and ATI serial handset interfaces used with accessible voting configurations.
components.caveat: The records identify certified or tested interface options; they do not establish which interface is connected to a fielded device.

components.name: Audio, sip-and-puff, and switch accessories
components.description: The certification records list named headphones, sip-and-puff devices, rocker or paddle switches, and a switch cable for accessible operation.
components.caveat: Listed alternatives do not establish that every accessory is supplied, connected, or used with every deployed ImageCast X setup.

components.name: Election media and activation cards
components.description: The reviewed test configuration lists ACOS-6-64 smart cards and named USB media used in the Democracy Suite configuration.
components.caveat: This groups source-listed removable media for navigation. It does not describe a jurisdiction's activation, programming, storage, or chain-of-custody procedure.

components.name: Optional transport and privacy accessories
components.description: The test plan lists ICX Classic and Prime transport bags, a privacy screen, a voting booth, and a Prime dual-bay battery charger as optional physical accessories.
modelNumbers: ICX Prime Battery Charger - Dual Bay
components.caveat: Optional accessories are not evidence of a jurisdiction's storage or setup procedure. The dual-bay charger is not represented as proof of an internal or external backup-power topology.

components.name: ICX Prime solid-state drive
components.description: An EAC-hosted advisory and Pro V&V ECO analysis identify an ICX Prime solid-state drive and an SSD-firmware update path for a bounded project-file installation or removal condition.
components.caveat: The records establish the component category but do not disclose a source-supported SSD model, firmware number, physical placement, cabling, or board-level arrangement, so it is not placed in the 3D scene.

versionObservations.caveat: This is the application version in the final certified configuration, not a live field reading and not a claim that it is the newest ICX release.

versionObservations.label: Certified ICX COTS operating environment
versionObservations.caveat: The scope establishes the evaluated environment, not a device's installed patch state or present field configuration.

versionObservations.caveat: This is a submitted test-plan version, not the final certified application version and not evidence of field use.

versionObservations.label: Final report ICX machine-configuration-file identifier
versionObservations.caveat: This is a named MCF identifier in the final test report, not an ICX application version, live readout, or field-installation record.

configurationChanges.description: The 5.17 modification set added ICX smart-card mutual authentication and secure messaging.
configurationChanges.caveat: This is certified configuration history relative to the 5.5-D baseline; it is not evidence that a jurisdiction installed or enabled the change.

configurationChanges.description: The 5.17 modification set added encryption of election databases on ICX and named companion devices.
configurationChanges.caveat: The source describes a bounded certification change, not a general security guarantee, field audit, or claim about every form of stored data.

configurationChanges.description: The 5.17 modification set added ICX support for provisional and Uniform Ballots, additional ballot-barcode information, and configurable on-screen contest columns.
configurationChanges.caveat: The record establishes the evaluated 5.17 modification set, not the election features configured or used by a jurisdiction.

configurationChanges.description: Pro V&V reviewed updated ICX Prime user-manual procedures for an SSD-firmware update path and classified the documentation change as de minimis with no additional 5.17 testing required.
configurationChanges.caveat: The records document a post-certification change path affecting federal 5.17, but do not name the SSD firmware version or establish adoption by any jurisdiction.

findings.title: No anomalies or deficiencies were reported in the 5.17 certification campaign
findings.description: The final Pro V&V report states that no anomalies and no deficiencies were encountered during the D-Suite 5.17 test campaign and recommends certification of the evaluated system.
findings.caveat: This statement is limited to that test campaign and evaluated configuration. It is not evidence that every field unit or later operating condition is defect-free.

findings.title: Touchscreen responsiveness advisory for named ICX Classic versions
findings.description: A May 2024 EAC-hosted manufacturer notice describes rare startup occasions when a named ICX Classic screen may not respond to touch and provides a power-cycle procedure.
findings.caveat: The notice names versions and jurisdictions but does not quantify occurrence or establish that every named jurisdiction or unit experienced the condition.

findings.title: ICX Prime SSD advisory and firmware-update documentation path
findings.description: An August 2024 advisory describes a bounded SSD error during election-project installation or removal, before logic-and-accuracy testing. The linked ECO records updated user-manual procedures for an SSD-firmware update path.
findings.caveat: The sources do not establish occurrence during an election, adoption of the update by a jurisdiction, or an SSD model or firmware number. Do not infer a field incident or effect on voted paper records.

findings.title: Straight-party and split-ticket selection review advisory
affectedSystemVersions: ImageCast X accessible BMD - advisory dated 2024-09-26
findings.description: An EAC-hosted customer notice describes a sequence in which previously removed selections can be reapplied after a straight-party selection is manually changed to split-ticket, and recommends review of the summary screen and printed ballot.
findings.caveat: The notice does not quantify field occurrence, identify an election outcome effect, or document a software resolution. It is not evidence of fraud, misconduct, or altered votes.

power.description: The SID-21V manual documents the optional battery model, chemistry, voltage, capacity, connector locations, and installation path. It does not publish an election-workload runtime.
power.caveat: This is an optional model-family component, not evidence that a particular certified or fielded ICX contains the battery or that its present capacity matches the specification.

power.description: The Pro V&V ICX configuration lists four external UPS alternatives. The reviewed sources do not state an ICX load-specific capacity or runtime.
power.caveat: Confirmed means the UPS models appear in the reviewed certified or test configuration, not that all are used together, that a jurisdiction selected one, or that battery health and runtime are known.

caveats: Certified and tested component alternatives are not evidence that all listed options are installed together or that a jurisdiction selected a particular option.
The 3D reference follows the SID-21V mechanical outline but remains a selection aid, not vendor CAD, a teardown, a wiring diagram, or proof of exact internal placement.
The SSD component category is source-supported, but its model, firmware number, physical location, and internal geometry remain unknown and are not visualized.
The UPS alternatives are confirmed configuration options, but capacity, load-specific runtime, maintenance condition, and field topology remain unknown.
Advisory notices are time-, version-, scenario-, and sometimes jurisdiction-scoped. They do not prove an election incident, altered votes, fraud, misconduct, or an incorrect outcome.

systems.summary: A source-linked pilot dossier for the DS200 within the EAC-certified EVS 6.4.0.0 configuration, with historical EAC change records and a separately labeled Washington deployment observation.

certification.caveat: EAC certification applies only to the evaluated EVS 6.4.0.0 certified configuration. It is not an endorsement, warranty, field inventory, or determination that a particular unit was operated in that configuration.

components.name: DS200 scanner and tabulator assembly
components.description: The certified scope describes the DS200 as a poll-place scanner and tabulator that scans voter selections from both sides of a ballot simultaneously.
components.caveat: Washington's state-approved configuration also lists hardware 1.3.13. No source in this pilot identifies the hardware revision of a particular county unit.

technicalSpecifications.label: Cellular modem option
technicalSpecifications.value: Separate modem board is optional where permitted; Rhode Island's 2021 procedure documents cellular transmission after polls close
technicalSpecifications.modelContext: DS200 model family; Rhode Island 2021 deployment procedure
technicalSpecifications.caveat: This establishes optional DS200 cellular capability and one jurisdiction's documented procedure. It does not mean every DS200 contains a modem, that EVS 6.4.0.0 permits WAN use, or that a modem was enabled or used in an unlisted jurisdiction.

technicalSpecifications.label: Cellular modem
technicalSpecifications.value: No WAN modem or WAN wireless use listed in the EVS 6.4.0.0 certified-system table
technicalSpecifications.caveat: This is a certified-system communications-use statement. It does not prove the physical absence of every connector or service component inside every DS200 unit.

technicalSpecifications.label: Ethernet / LAN
technicalSpecifications.value: No LAN TCP/IP or LAN wireless use listed in the EVS 6.4.0.0 certified-system table
technicalSpecifications.caveat: This establishes permitted certified-system communications use, not a teardown-based count of physical RJ-45 connectors.

technicalSpecifications.label: Physical USB port count
technicalSpecifications.caveat: Reviewed certification artifacts identify removable media and system components but do not publish a DS200 physical USB-connector count.

technicalSpecifications.label: Installed RAM
technicalSpecifications.caveat: No reviewed artifact publishes the installed RAM technology or capacity for the certified DS200 configurations.

components.name: Ballot scanning path
components.description: The public certification scope establishes simultaneous front-and-back ballot scanning. The schematic path is illustrative and does not reproduce proprietary internal drawings.
components.caveat: Public sources document the function, not the exact internal shape or placement shown in the schematic.

components.name: Display and touchscreen assembly
components.description: ECO 1042 identifies a touchscreen controller, LCD, mounting bracket, LVDS cables, and a field-service display subassembly in DS200 hardware configuration 1.3.11.
components.caveat: This historical ECO identifies a DS200-family configuration change. It does not prove that the illustrated assembly is present in an EVS 6.4.0.0 fielded unit.

technicalSpecifications.label: Processor architecture
technicalSpecifications.value: Quad-core processor
technicalSpecifications.caveat: The approved change identifies the core count but not the processor manufacturer, model, clock speed, or the configuration of a particular fielded unit.

technicalSpecifications.label: Exact CPU model
technicalSpecifications.caveat: The reviewed ECO analysis does not name an exact processor part number.

components.name: Processor module
components.description: ECO 1042 records a move to a quad-core processor on the motherboard for DS200 hardware configuration 1.3.11.
components.caveat: Processor make, model, location, and presence in a particular EVS 6.4.0.0 fielded unit are not publicly confirmed by this pilot.

components.name: Scanner board and FPGA logic
components.description: ECO 1035 documents a DS200 scanner-board FPGA-code update intended to improve thermal stability and calibration resolution; ECO 1042 also references a board change for a new motor driver.
components.caveat: The public records do not identify a board part number or establish the board/FPGA revision installed in a particular EVS 6.4.0.0 unit.

components.name: Ballot container options
components.description: The EVS 6.4.0.0 scope lists multiple DS200/DS300-compatible ballot boxes, tote bins, a trolley, tote bag, and carrying cases as proprietary configuration components.
components.caveat: These are permitted configuration options, not a claim that every DS200 uses every listed container or accessory.

components.name: Tote-bin security gasketing
components.description: ECO 1165 adds a security gasketing kit intended to prevent cards or ballots from entering through gaps along the tote-bin hinge area.
components.caveat: The change was approved for EVS 6.4.0.0, but the pilot has no evidence that a particular jurisdiction installed the kit.

components.name: Exterior seal area
components.description: ECO 983 documents a historical DS200 hardware 1.3.10.0 exterior seal-area change.
components.caveat: This record does not establish inclusion in EVS 6.4.0.0 or installation on any fielded unit.

components.name: Battery backup and internal power
components.description: The ES&S one-sheet states that the DS200 has battery backup. The reviewed sources do not identify its battery chemistry, manufacturer, model, capacity, runtime, or internal placement.
components.caveat: Battery-backup presence is manufacturer-documented, but no reviewed source supports a battery model, capacity, runtime, chemistry, or scene placement. Central-count UPS models must not be transferred to the DS200.

technicalSpecifications.label: Backup supply
technicalSpecifications.value: Battery backup documented; model, chemistry, capacity, and runtime not stated
technicalSpecifications.caveat: The one-sheet confirms battery-backup presence only. It does not disclose a battery part number or unit-level condition.

versionObservations.label: EAC-certified firmware
versionObservations.caveat: This is the firmware in the certified EVS 6.4.0.0 configuration, not a live reading from a deployed unit and not a claim about the newest EVS family firmware.

versionObservations.label: Washington-approved firmware
versionObservations.caveat: Washington's approved configuration is not a county device inspection.

versionObservations.label: Washington-approved hardware revisions
versionObservations.caveat: The state record lists approved revisions; it does not identify which revision a county deployed.

configurationChanges.description: Exterior seal-area change for DS200 hardware 1.3.10.0.
configurationChanges.caveat: The record does not establish inclusion in the EVS 6.4.0.0 baseline or local installation.

configurationChanges.description: End-of-life replacements and related DS200 hardware 1.3.11 changes: touchscreen controller, LCD/bracket/LVDS cables, display service subassembly, quad-core processor, scanner-board motor-driver accommodation, and USB-hub power-cable wire gauge.
configurationChanges.caveat: The ECO documents an approved historical configuration change, not the internals of every DS200 or an EVS 6.4.0.0 deployment.

configurationChanges.description: Scanner-board FPGA-code update described as improving thermal stability and calibration resolution.
configurationChanges.caveat: The source does not identify the board or FPGA revision installed in a particular EVS 6.4.0.0 unit.

configurationChanges.description: Ballot-box change adding a ballot-bag option.
configurationChanges.caveat: An approved accessory option does not establish use by a particular jurisdiction.

configurationChanges.description: Collapsible ballot-box change adding a ballot-trolley/binning option.
configurationChanges.caveat: An approved accessory option does not establish use by a particular jurisdiction.

configurationChanges.description: Tote-bin security gasketing intended to prevent cards or ballots from entering through hinge-area gaps; Pro V&V states the change was reviewed and functionally tested and requires no firmware/software change.
configurationChanges.caveat: EVS 6.4.0.0 is listed as affected, but local installation is not established.

findings.title: Pro V&V anomaly status
findings.description: The certification test report states that no anomalies occurred during the EVS 6.4.0.0 test campaign.
findings.caveat: This is scoped to the submitted test campaign. It is not a claim that the system has no bugs or that no field incident can occur.

findings.title: Deficiencies described but not itemized
findings.description: The public report says encountered deficiencies were tracked and resolutions verified as needed, but section 3.3 does not itemize those deficiencies.
findings.caveat: Do not infer the number, severity, affected component, or field impact of non-enumerated test deficiencies.

findings.title: Previously scanned ballot is not automatically distinguished
findings.description: Washington's staff report states that EVS 6.4.0.0 cannot distinguish whether a ballot was previously scanned and describes ballot-handling and staffing controls recommended by ES&S.
findings.caveat: This is an operational limitation and mitigation note, not evidence that duplicate scanning occurred in an election.

findings.title: No advisory attachment listed on selected EAC record
findings.description: The archived EAC EVS 6.4.0.0 record did not list an advisory attachment when retrieved on 2026-07-19.
findings.caveat: This is a page-listing observation, not a claim that no advisories, bugs, vulnerabilities, service bulletins, or field incidents exist.

power.description: The ES&S one-sheet confirms DS200 battery backup. The certification and state records reviewed here do not publish the battery manufacturer, model, chemistry, capacity, runtime, condition, or jurisdiction power topology.
power.caveat: Confirmed battery-backup presence must not be expanded into an inferred model, runtime, internal location, service condition, or claim about external site power.

deployments.caveat: The state table confirms the EVS version at county grain, not DS200 use, unit count, firmware, hardware revision, ECO installation, or power configuration.

caveats: Certified configuration is not the same as field deployment. A county system-version record does not establish the components, firmware, hardware revision, or change orders installed on each unit.
The photo-informed 3D schematic is a selection aid, not vendor CAD, a teardown, an engineering drawing, or proof of exact dimensions or internal placement.
Public findings are presented with version and source scope. A missing advisory listing is not evidence that no bug, vulnerability, incident, or service bulletin exists.
The manufacturer documents DS200 battery backup, but its model, chemistry, capacity, runtime, internal placement, condition, and county-level power topology remain unknown.
